Title: Policies for information security
Justification: Required by clause 5.2; clients' contracts and DORA expect a policy set
How implemented or planned: AI use and governance policy in force; information security policy to follow the SoA

Title: Information security roles and responsibilities
Justification: Five teams and a separate governance and risk office need clear duties
How implemented or planned: Roles defined in the scope; Governance and Risk Office reports to the Group CRO so it can challenge

Title: Segregation of duties
Justification: AI outputs and platform changes must not be approved by the person who made them
How implemented or planned: Analyst approval separate from drafting; Terraform applied from a reviewed plan

Title: Management responsibilities
Justification: Head of Sextant owns the scope and must enforce policy
How implemented or planned: AI Risk Committee approves systems and changes; scope owner named

Title: Contact with authorities
Justification: CERT-In reporting in India; clients' regulators reached through contracts
How implemented or planned: Contact list held by the Governance and Risk Office; client contracts route regulator contact

Title: Contact with special interest groups
Justification: AI security threats change quickly
How implemented or planned: Membership of cloud and AI security forums to be recorded

Title: Threat intelligence
Justification: Prompt injection and AWS threats evolve; operations agents read untrusted logs
How implemented or planned: Threat feed review feeding red-team cases for the agents

Title: Information security in project management
Justification: Every new agent, tool or client is a project with security impact
How implemented or planned: Decision records with alternatives and consequences; AI Risk Committee gate

Title: Inventory of information and other associated assets
Justification: Risks and controls must name the assets they protect
How implemented or planned: Asset inventory and AI system inventory maintained

Title: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
Justification: Staff use of personal AI tools is a Critical inherent risk
How implemented or planned: Data-to-tool rules in the AI use policy; group acceptable use policy

Title: Return of assets
Justification: Staff leave with laptops and tokens
How implemented or planned: Group leaver process; Sextant revokes AWS access same day

Title: Classification of information
Justification: Client content needs a higher protection level than internal records
How implemented or planned: Four-level scheme applied to every asset

Title: Labelling of information
Justification: Labels must follow client content into knowledge bases and outputs
How implemented or planned: Client tag on every chunk and resource; AI outputs labelled as AI-drafted

Title: Information transfer
Justification: Answers and evidence packs leave Sextant for clients
How implemented or planned: Delivery only through each client's agreed channel; transfer rules in contracts

Title: Access control
Justification: Access to client content must be per client and least privilege
How implemented or planned: IAM groups in the lab; per-client attribute checks at retrieval designed

Title: Identity management
Justification: Every action must trace to one person
How implemented or planned: Named IAM user, no shared accounts; tutorial users deleted (F-03)

Title: Authentication information
Justification: Stolen credentials expose every client
How implemented or planned: MFA on root (two devices) and admin; no access keys anywhere

Title: Access rights
Justification: Rights must be reviewed as people and clients change
How implemented or planned: Groups-based rights in the lab; quarterly access review planned

Title: Information security in supplier relationships
Justification: AWS and model providers process client content
How implemented or planned: Supplier review of security and model terms before approval

Title: Addressing information security within supplier agreements
Justification: DORA Art. 30 requires specific contract terms down the chain
How implemented or planned: Required clauses checked for each supplier; flowed down from client contracts

Title: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
Justification: Model providers sit behind Bedrock: a supply chain within a supply chain
How implemented or planned: Model terms (training on inputs, retention, region) checked quarterly

Title: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
Justification: A supplier restriction has already stopped model access (F-06)
How implemented or planned: Supplier changes tracked; F-06 led to MIC-DEC-012; subcontractor register planned

Title: Information security for use of cloud services
Justification: The whole platform runs on AWS
How implemented or planned: Region choice, residency rules, budgets excluding credits, keyless access

Title: Information security incident management planning and preparation
Justification: DORA and CERT-In set short reporting deadlines
How implemented or planned: Incident plan with client and regulator timelines; AI incidents included

Title: Assessment and decision on information security events
Justification: Not every alert is an incident; root activity must be explained
How implemented or planned: Root sign-ins reviewed and explained against CloudTrail

Title: Response to information security incidents
Justification: Response steps needed for data leaks into AI tools and wrong AI outputs
How implemented or planned: Playbooks to be written for the AI incident types in MIC-POL-001

Title: Learning from information security incidents
Justification: Findings must change practice
How implemented or planned: Each finding recorded with its resolution and the practice it changed

Title: Collection of evidence
Justification: Clients' auditors must be able to rely on evidence
How implemented or planned: Evidence fingerprinted with SHA-256 and kept byte-exact

Title: Information security during disruption
Justification: Banks depend on Sextant during their own incidents
How implemented or planned: Security controls kept in degraded modes; manual fallback for agents

Title: ICT readiness for business continuity
Justification: DORA treats Sextant as supporting critical functions
How implemented or planned: Exit plan and second-provider design for the model layer

Title: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
Justification: Ten regimes across three jurisdictions apply
How implemented or planned: Requirements listed per client and framework in the scope

Title: Intellectual property rights
Justification: Clients' documents and licensed standards are used in retrieval
How implemented or planned: Licensed standards used under licence; client content used only for that client

Title: Protection of records
Justification: Evidence and logs are records clients rely on
How implemented or planned: Byte-exact evidence files; Object Lock planned for log storage

Title: Privacy and protection of PII
Justification: GDPR and DPDP apply to personal data in client material
How implemented or planned: Residency at jurisdiction level; no client data used for training

Title: Independent review of information security
Justification: Group Internal Audit and client audits will test Sextant
How implemented or planned: Group Internal Audit review planned after the first SoA cycle

Title: Compliance with policies, rules and standards for information security
Justification: Policy without checking is not a control
How implemented or planned: Monthly checks of deployed tools and AI service use against the inventory

Title: Documented operating procedures
Justification: Repeatable operation and evidence need written steps
How implemented or planned: Working method documented; Terraform runbook in lab README

Title: Screening
Justification: Staff access bank material
How implemented or planned: Group pre-employment screening; client-required checks added per contract

Title: Terms and conditions of employment
Justification: Security and AI duties must be contractual
How implemented or planned: Group employment terms; AI use policy acknowledged on joining

Title: Information security awareness, education and training
Justification: AI misuse by staff is a Critical inherent risk; EU AI Act Art. 4
How implemented or planned: AI literacy on joining and yearly; reviewer training on automation bias

Title: Disciplinary process
Justification: Policy breaches need consequences
How implemented or planned: Group disciplinary process referenced by the AI use policy

Title: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
Justification: Confidentiality continues after leaving
How implemented or planned: Group terms; AWS access revoked on the last day

Title: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements
Justification: Client contracts require confidentiality of staff
How implemented or planned: Group NDAs; client-specific NDAs where required

Title: Remote working
Justification: Client work is done only from secure client bays
How implemented or planned: Client content not accessible outside client bays and managed devices

Title: Information security event reporting
Justification: Staff must report AI data leaks the same day
How implemented or planned: Same-day reporting route in the AI use policy

Title: Physical security perimeters
Justification: Client bays hold endpoints with access to client content
How implemented or planned: Meridian group facility perimeter (simulated); AWS data centres under shared responsibility

Title: Physical entry
Justification: Only authorised staff may enter client bays
How implemented or planned: Group badge access to client bays (simulated)

Title: Securing offices, rooms and facilities
Justification: Client bays are segregated work areas
How implemented or planned: Group facility controls (simulated)

Title: Physical security monitoring
Justification: Client contracts may require monitored bays
How implemented or planned: Group CCTV and monitoring (simulated)

Title: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
Justification: Pune facility and AWS regions face environmental risk
How implemented or planned: Group facility controls; AWS for data centres

Title: Working in secure areas
Justification: Rules needed inside client bays
How implemented or planned: No personal devices in client bays (group rule, simulated)

Title: Clear desk and clear screen
Justification: Client material visible on screens
How implemented or planned: Group clear-desk policy; screen lock on managed devices

Title: Equipment siting and protection
Justification: Endpoints in client bays
How implemented or planned: Group facility controls (simulated)

Title: Security of assets off-premises
Justification: Laptops may leave the floor
How implemented or planned: Group device encryption and loss reporting

Title: Storage media
Justification: Removable media could carry client content out
How implemented or planned: USB storage blocked on client-bay endpoints (group, simulated)

Title: Supporting utilities
Justification: Power and cooling for the floor; AWS facilities
How implemented or planned: Group facility; AWS under shared responsibility

Title: Cabling security
Justification: Network cabling to client bays
How implemented or planned: Group facility controls (simulated)

Title: Equipment maintenance
Justification: Endpoints and network equipment need maintenance
How implemented or planned: Group IT maintenance

Title: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
Justification: Disposed endpoints may hold client content
How implemented or planned: Group certified disposal; AWS media sanitisation under shared responsibility

Title: User endpoint devices
Justification: Endpoints are where staff could leak data to AI tools
How implemented or planned: Group device management; Sextant adds AI upload blocking and extension allow-list

Title: Privileged access rights
Justification: Administrator access reaches every client
How implemented or planned: Root used only for root-only tasks and reconciled against CloudTrail; time-limited elevation planned

Title: Information access restriction
Justification: Client A must never see client B
How implemented or planned: One knowledge base and graph per client; attribute check at retrieval

Title: Access to source code
Justification: Infrastructure code must not be changed by unauthorised people
How implemented or planned: Repository write access limited to the author; code is public by design, state never committed

Title: Secure authentication
Justification: Password-only access to AWS would expose all clients
How implemented or planned: MFA everywhere; `aws login` sessions; no long-lived keys

Title: Capacity management
Justification: Clients rely on availability during their incidents
How implemented or planned: Service quotas and usage monitored; budgets alert on spend

Title: Protection against malware
Justification: Endpoints and uploaded client files
How implemented or planned: Group endpoint protection; client documents scanned on ingestion (designed)

Title: Management of technical vulnerabilities
Justification: Platform and dependencies need patching
How implemented or planned: Dependency and image scanning in the CI pipeline

Title: Configuration management
Justification: Misconfiguration is the main cloud failure mode
How implemented or planned: Infrastructure defined in Terraform with pinned versions; Checkov planned

Title: Information deletion
Justification: Client content must be deleted when a contract ends
How implemented or planned: Per-client deletion on exit, recorded as evidence

Title: Data masking
Justification: Logs and tickets read by agents may contain personal data
How implemented or planned: Personal data redacted from agent inputs and stored logs where not needed

Title: Data leakage prevention
Justification: Client data in personal AI tools is the highest-rated risk
How implemented or planned: Upload blocking to unapproved AI services; egress allow-list for the platform

Title: Information backup
Justification: Knowledge bases and evidence must survive loss
How implemented or planned: Versioned, in-region backups; restore tested

Title: Redundancy of information processing facilities
Justification: Active-active within a jurisdiction is the target design
How implemented or planned: Second region per jurisdiction in target design; not built in the lab

Title: Logging
Justification: Auditors and clients must be able to see who did what
How implemented or planned: CloudTrail in the lab; 180-day log copy in Mumbai designed (CERT-In)

Title: Monitoring activities
Justification: Root use and unusual activity must be noticed
How implemented or planned: Automated root-activity report; budget alerts

Title: Clock synchronization
Justification: Log timelines must line up across sources
How implemented or planned: AWS time sources; endpoints synchronised by group IT

Title: Use of privileged utility programs
Justification: Admin tooling can bypass controls
How implemented or planned: Admin tooling runs only through `aws login` as a named user

Title: Installation of software on operational systems
Justification: Agents and platform components must be approved
How implemented or planned: Only pipeline-deployed, approved components; tool allow-list for agents

Title: Networks security
Justification: Platform traffic must stay private
How implemented or planned: Private networking and endpoints in the platform build

Title: Security of network services
Justification: Model and AWS service calls cross service boundaries
How implemented or planned: Private endpoints to AWS services; no public model endpoints

Title: Segregation of networks
Justification: Client environments must be separated
How implemented or planned: Per-client segregation in the platform build

Title: Web filtering
Justification: Blocks unapproved AI sites from client bays
How implemented or planned: Proxy categories block unapproved AI services

Title: Use of cryptography
Justification: Client content at rest and in transit
How implemented or planned: AWS default encryption at rest; customer-managed keys per client designed

Title: Secure development life cycle
Justification: The platform and agents are built in-house
How implemented or planned: Security and AI review gates before release

Title: Application security requirements
Justification: Agents need explicit limits
How implemented or planned: Read-only tools; deny-by-default Cedar policies; citation requirement

Title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
Justification: Residency and client separation are architectural
How implemented or planned: Jurisdiction-level residency; one store per client; keyless access

Title: Secure coding
Justification: Platform code handles untrusted input from logs and documents
How implemented or planned: Code review; untrusted tool output treated as data

Title: Security testing in development and acceptance
Justification: Controls must be proven, not assumed
How implemented or planned: Terraform lab attacked and proven; red-team and canary tests for AI designed

Title: Outsourced development
Justification: Sextant builds its platform with its own staff; no development is outsourced
How implemented or planned: Re-assess if any development is outsourced

Title: Separation of development, test and production environments
Justification: Test data must never be live client content
How implemented or planned: Separate environments in target design; lab is a single test account (MIC-DEC-007)

Title: Change management
Justification: Unapproved changes could widen agent permissions
How implemented or planned: Changes applied only from a reviewed Terraform plan; AI changes need committee approval

Title: Test information
Justification: Tests must not use real client data
How implemented or planned: Synthetic and fixed sample data only (MIC-DEC-012)

Title: Protection of information systems during audit testing
Justification: Client audits and Internal Audit will test the platform
How implemented or planned: Read-only audit access, agreed in advance, logged
